items.title: Introducing Vercel Board
items.text: Software development is moving from individual agents completing tasks to teams of agents working on more complex projects. A single agent can track its work in a Markdown file, but there isn't a purpose-built primitive for tracking tasks, delegation, statuses, logs, and completed work across many agents and subagents. We ran into this coordination problem internally and started experimenting with a shared message board as a primitive on two key projects: Along the way, we added multiple features like grants for different levels of access (for humans and agents), two-way sync for multiple tools (like Slack), and a lot more. Today we are launching Vercel Board as an experimental agentic primitive. It packages what we've learned about coordinating work across agent fleets and builds towards a future where multiple teams of humans and agents orchestrate swarms, software factories, and other agentic workflows. We built Board for our own needs, but invite curious developers to test it alongside us and give feedback. It is harness agnostic and fits well into existing multi-agent reinforcement learning. items.text: Today we’re launching , a six-week accelerator for AI founders at the idea and pre-seed stages.Vercel X Join a cohort of 40 teams at our San Francisco HQ and build alongside Vercel’s product leaders, designers, and engineers. The program takes no equity for participation and offers access to a program-wide pool of more than $9M in credits from Vercel, AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, and other partners. Applications are now open through November 29, 2026. The program runs from January 19 to March 2, 2027. Vercel has worked with more than 100 early-stage teams from around the world across three accelerator cohorts. Alumni include , Alloy Robotics, , , and . items.title: MITRE Acknowledges Inaccurate Publication Timestamps in 87% of Its Recent CVE Records
items.text: MITRE has acknowledged that a legacy publishing system is responsible for inaccurate timestamps in thousands of CVE records, following research showing that 87% of the organization's CVEs published over the past year were assigned a publication time of exactly midnight UTC. MITRE says the legacy system responsible for the problem will be phased out in the first quarter of 2027. The findings come from security researcher Jerry Gamblin, founder of RogoLabs, an independent open source research lab focused on vulnerability intelligence. His projects include the CNA Scorecard, which evaluates the completeness of CVE records, and CNAPulse, which tracks vulnerability publishing activity across CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs). Socket has previously covered both projects and Gamblin's broader research into CVE data quality. Analyzing CVE records published over the 52 weeks ending November 16, 2026, Gamblin found that 3,901 of MITRE's 4,509 CVEs (87%) had a datePublished timestamp of exactly 00:00:00.000Z.
